news.title: ‘Doesn’t have the support’: FIFA boss put on notice as stunning leadership challenge looms
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has been delivered a stunning warning over his future, with UEFA chief Aleksander Ceferin declaring he must recognise he has lost the support of the football world or prepare to face a leadership challenge. Infantino has come under increasing pressure over his controversial and now-abandoned proposal to secure private investment in FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup. The saga has created an extraordinary divide within world football, with UEFA threatening a boycott of FIFA competitions and several continental and national federations withdrawing their support for the 56-year-old.

news.title: Infantino announces launch of Under-15 World Cup with 211 teams taking part
news.lede: "It will be like a festival for children". Gianni Infantino has confirmed that the International Federation of Association Football (FIFA) will organise the first-ever Under-15 World Cup this year, open to all 211 member associations. Talk of the project had been swirling in recent weeks. Now the FIFA president has publicly committed to making it happen.

news.title: Diego Maradona's 'Hand of God' football from 1986 World Cup win over England sells for £2.5m
news.lede: The 'Hand of God' football was previously sold in 2022. The football with which Diego Maradona scored his famous 'hand of God' goal at the 1986 World Cup has sold at auction for £2.5m. Maradona famously punched the ball past goalkeeper Peter Shilton in Argentina's 2-1 quarter-final win over England. After the game, he told reporters it had been scored "a little with the head of Maradona and a little with the hand of God".

news.title: CommBank Junior Matildas Gear Up for U-17 World Cup
news.lede: The CommBank Junior Matildas will assemble for their final domestic training camp ahead of FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup Morocco 2026™, with Australia's debut in the tournament set to kick off on October 19th against Chile. CommBank Junior Matildas Head Coach, Michael Cooper, has called in a 28-player squad for the upcoming training camp, as his coaching staff have their final opportunity to make selection choices ahead of the squad announcement for the upcoming FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup Morocco 2026™. Australia qualified for the first-ever time for the showpiece U-17 event following the team's fourth-place finish at the AFC U-17 Women's Asian Cup 2026™, with the tournament set to provide invaluable experience for Australia's next generation of stars.

news.title: Rodri capture can catapult Barcelona back to very top of European game: GOAL grades the biggest deals of the 2026 summer transfer window
news.lede: For some football fans, the summer is the part of the calendar that they look forward to the most - and that's not just because it's filled by a World Cup every four years! Rather, it's because the end of the season means only one thing: It's time for transfers! The 2026 window is once again proving to be busy, with some huge names making big-money moves before deadline day on September 1. We know that some transfers turn out well for all parties involved, but there are plenty where at least one of the clubs, or even the player, are left wondering what might have been had they made a different decision while at the negotiating table.

news.title: Spain's World Cup hero Torres saves PSG's blushes at Rennes
news.lede: Spain's World Cup winner Ferran Torres scored twice to claim a draw for Paris Saint-Germain as they started the defence of their French Ligue 1 title with a 2-2 draw at Rennes. Torres came off the bench for his Ligue 1 debut and opened his account for his new club weeks on from scoring the winning goal for La Roja in the World Cup final. Rennes led at the break after Sebastian Szymanski and Esteban Lepaul scored at Roazhon Park before Torres' clinical interventions thanks to assists from fellow World Cup winner Fabian Ruiz. news.title: Ceferin rules out Fifa presidency bid but claims Infantino could face challenger
news.lede: Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin ruled himself out of running for the Fifa presidency but said Gianni ⁠Infantino would likely face a ⁠challenger if he seeks re-election next year following ⁠a global backlash over a plan to sell part of the World Cup to private investors. Speaking to The Rest Is Politics: Leading podcast, which will air on Monday, Ceferin said he was not interested in succeeding Infantino despite growing uncertainty around the Fifa president’s future after his abandoned investment proposal. “One reason is that I love Uefa ‌and I love working here, and I think that at a certain point you have also, I mean, it’s time also to enjoy life a bit,” Ceferin said. And the second point is, my credibility is much, much, much higher if I’m not interested in the position.”
